newsitem.title: UK: GDR REPORT - India firmer in thin trade.
newsitem.headline: GDR REPORT - India firmer in thin trade.

text.p: Indian global despositary receipts (GDRs) saw further gains on Friday, albeit at a slower pace than Thursday, but trade was slow.
"We have seen more buy orders coming in over the last two or three days but the market is still sorting itself out," said a trader.
The HSBC James Capel Indian GDR index JCEAI closed up 0.60 points at 61.96 points, with the premium over the local market at 11.76 percent compared with yesterday's 10.57 percent.
The Bombay Stock Exchange 30-share index fell 15.21 points, or 0.48 percent to 3,148.57.
India's biggest truck maker Tata Engineering and Locomotive Company Ltd Net first half net profit rose to 3,305.3 rupees from 2,265.3.
"The earnings were ahead of expactations," said a trader.
Bajaj Auto continued gains after yesterday's 27 percent rise in first half net profit to 2.26 billion rupees.
After a $1.83 rise yesterday, the stock rose $1.00 to $32.50/$33.50.
Indian Hotels was also stronger, up 63 cents to $23.75/$24.75.

"There was a turning point in mid-October when there were good selling volumes matched by good buying. Now the selling has dried up and buy orders are taking a little longer to be filled," said the trader.

The Capel Korea GDR Index ended up 1.70 points, or 2.64 percent, at 66.15, a premium of 28.46 percent over the local market after the Korea Composite Index rose 10.28 points to provisionally end at 767.87.
The Capel Taiwan GDR Index ended up 1.21 points, or 1.39 percent, at 88.38, a premium of 2.21 percent after the Taiwan Weighted Index rose 29.02 points, 0.45 percent, to 6,455.11
